context:
This is a textbook vertical-slice refactor (SHARED/slicing-framework.md).
For each slice:
  1. Move a cohesive group of methods to the new module
  2. Re-export from adapter.py: `from .connection import *` (with __all__)
  3. Run uv run -- python -m pytest -m fast -q  → must pass
  4. Run cross-platform validation suite        → must pass
  5. Commit with prefix `refactor(platforms/base):`
  6. Push, confirm CI green, then proceed to next slice

ZERO adapter implementation file may be modified beyond import lines (and
only if absolutely required, which it shouldn't be given re-exports).
description:
Quality plan Phase 3. benchbox/platforms/base/adapter.py is 5,158 lines -
the single largest non-generated file in the repo and the foundation
underlying all 73 adapter implementations. Its size makes review,
navigation, and safe modification difficult; bugs here have maximum
blast radius.

Split by responsibility (NOT by size) into focused modules behind a
re-export shim, so all 73 adapter implementations keep their imports
unchanged. Vertical slices: extract one submodule per slice, run full
cross-platform validation between slices, commit per slice.

The read-only mapping work lives in a separate prep TODO
(quality-map-adapter-base-refactor-scope) so analysis can start early while
code-moving work remains blocked on the safety nets.

Proposed split:
  base/adapter.py          (Protocol/ABC only - ~400 lines)
  base/connection.py       (Connection lifecycle, retries - ~600 lines)
  base/execution.py        (Query execution, timing wrap - ~800 lines)
  base/data_loading.py     (Native + external table modes - ~900 lines)
  base/result_capture.py   (Status, errors, plans - ~600 lines)
  base/dialect_translation.py (sqlglot integration - ~700 lines)
  base/tuning.py           (Tuning hook resolution - ~500 lines)

anti_patterns.dont: collapse multiple slices into one commit
anti_patterns.why: review and rollback need slice-level granularity

anti_patterns.dont: extract while adapters or tests are in flight on other branches

anti_patterns.instead: preserve names exactly even if they're imperfect

preserves.behavior: ALL 73 adapter implementations import from `benchbox.platforms.base.adapter` unchanged
All existing platform-specific tests pass after every slice (≥21,000 tests)
Cross-platform validation suite (from quality-add-cross-platform-result-validation) passes after every slice
Public protocol surface of PlatformAdapter (every @abstractmethod, every public attribute) is byte-identical
Timing semantics (mono_time vs wall-clock) preserved exactly per timing policy

verifications.description: Full fast test suite passes after every slice

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c 'from benchbox.core.platform_registry import PlatformRegistry; print(len(PlatformRegistry.get_available_platforms()))'
verifications.description: Platform registry still enumerates adapters after each slice
verifications.expected: prints a positive platform count with no error
